text:
maria: ok kicking off a short sync on the tiered fallback policy — we need to lock scope and launch criteria by EOD Friday. customers + infra constraints in play.
jon: goal is clear: deterministic routing that prefers cheaper variants but preserves required features (function-calling, deterministic tokens) per customer tier.
ash (ash): fyi — FinCo and HealthApp flagged this as blocker for Dedicated onboarding. they need model pinning + auditable fallback reasons.
sam: infra reality check: cross-region capacity for 8-bit variants is limited. we can do region-aware routing but might need reserved pools for gold customers.
nora: ML note: quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) sometimes break structured output and function-calling. we should enumerate incompatible ops in the spec.
lee: SRE asks we add explicit circuit-breaker thresholds and a fast-fail path to avoid cascading retries. acceptance criteria should include alert runbook links.
maria: propose minimum scope: (1) tier definitions (free/std/gold/enterprise), (2) region affinity rules, (3) compatibility matrix for model features, (4) fallback audit events. anything missing?
jon: add rollout controls: canary percent, automatic rollback on quality regressions, and a config to force model pinning per customer.
ash (ash): also need SLA language for Dedicated customers — guaranteed fallback to pinned variant or manual failover within X mins.
sam: question on enforcement: do we want routing policy in control plane only or a small on-host verifier to avoid incompatible dispatches? on-host verifier costs CPU but reduces bad dispatches.
nora: on-host verifier could run a lightweight feature-check (supports_functions, max_sequence) before enqueuing. I'll sketch API for compatibility checks.
lee: acceptance checklist suggestion:
- nonregression test that failing fallback doesn't increase p99 latency by >20%
- alerts for "fallback surge" (>1000/min)
- audit log schema documented

maria: thanks — I'll capture that. next: edge cases we must specify. suggestions?
jon: edge cases: model family mismatch (decoder vs encoder-decoder), incompatible tokenizer leading to crash, downstream function-call schema mismatch. define safe-default: reject fallback and surface clear error.
nora: also handle partial-output cases: if fallback produces truncated structured output, caller must get explicit "degraded": true flag. doc that in response contract.
ash (ash): customers will want opt-out flags for auto-fallback. spec needs per-customer toggle + admin audit trail.
sam: resource edge: what if fallback capacity is exhausted? fallback-of-fallback: route to hosted lowest-tier model and tag response with "fallback_chain": [a,b,c]. ok?
lee: agree, but cap chain length to 3 and mark with trace id.
maria: acceptance criteria draft (we can edit):
- routing respects per-customer pinning 100% of the time when set
- fallbacks only used when primary variant unavailable or degraded
- audit events emitted with reason, chosen_variant, latency, trace_id
- circuit-breaker prevents >5x retry storms for same customer within 1m
- behavioral tests for function-calling and structured output across supported model variants

jon: small config example for spec: 
```
route_policy:{
  tiers:["free","std","gold","enterprise"],
  region_affinity:{eu:["v2-8bit","v1"],us:["v2-8bit","v1"]},
  compatibility_checks:["supports_functions","tokenizer_family_match"],
  max_fallback_chain:3
}
```

maria: next steps: jon + nora to draft compatibility matrix, sam to propose infra cost for reserved pools, lee to write SRE acceptance tests, ash to collect customer opt-out requirements. i'll create a PRD stub and link tickets.
deploy-bot: Created ticket INF-5412 in JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-5412
jon: I'll open a short RFC doc and ping reviewers. aiming for review by Wed.
lee: quick note — include perf budget per tier (p95 <= X ms) so routing decisions can consider latency cost tradeoffs.
maria: agreed. thanks everyone. follow-ups in the RFC thread. :thumbsup:
